pathway.title: TELUS CORP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, leverage is the central issue and depends on definition. Net debt of C$ 25,963 million over LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs of C$ 7,315 million is 3.55x unrounded (3.5x as reported), above the issuer's new 2.5x to 3.0x objective range, and below the 4.25x covenant limit by 0.70x on the issuer's own measure. The issuer gives one-half equity credit to its junior subordinated notes; gross debt of C$ 31,456 million is 4.30x LTM EBITDA, and before the equity credit net debt was 4.02x at March 31, 2026. The covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is indicative [CP-1: Chart data leverage; Definitions review].

Second, cash interest cover is declining. LTM EBITDA over cash interest paid was 4.62x at June 30, 2026, 5.09x at March 31, 2026 and 5.31x at FY2025. Interest paid rose on 2025 junior subordinated issuance, a promissory note and a C$ 51 million prepayment premium, so part of the fall is one-off; the issuer's own coverage measure is 4.9x against a 2.00x covenant floor [CP-1: Chart data interest cover].

Third, liquidity is adequate; refinancing relies on market access. Cash is C$ 1,387 million, revolver availability C$ 657 million after a C$ 2,093 million commercial paper backstop, securitization availability C$ 680 million and a non-revolving facility C$ 344 million. Current maturities of long-term debt are C$ 3,802 million and include commercial paper that the revolver supports. The maturity schedule, dated March 31, 2026, shows C$ 3,148 million falling due in the rest of 2026, C$ 1,928 million in 2027 and C$ 2,319 million in 2028 [CP-1: Chart data liquidity and debt maturities].

Fourth, earnings and guidance weakened in the quarter. Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was C$ 1,777 million against C$ 1,812 million, with a net loss of C$ 1,830 million after a C$ 2,135 million non-cash TELUS Digital impairment, which does not touch covenants. Management lowered 2026 guidance: service revenue flat to a 2 per cent decline, Adjusted EBITDA down 2 to 4 per cent, free cash flow about C$ 1.8 billion from about C$ 2.45 billion, and capital expenditures about C$ 2.6 billion from about C$ 2.3 billion (Management Language) [CP-1: Subsequent events and guidance].

Fifth, the deleveraging plan rests on management actions rather than organic cash flow. The quarterly dividend was reset to C$ 0.1875 per share from C$ 0.4184, with management estimating about C$ 2.7 billion of cash savings through 2028; the 3.0x target date moved from year-end 2027 to year-end 2028 and the objective range moved from 2.2x to 2.7x to 2.5x to 3.0x. Asset sales of TELUS Health non-core assets and real estate are under way with no assets, prices or timing supplied [CP-1A: Capital allocation; Conflicts].

Sixth, the perimeter changed in 2025 and structural position is incomplete. TELUS bought out the TELUS Digital minority on October 31, 2025 and sold minority equity in the Terrion tower partnership for net cash proceeds of C$ 1,246 million while keeping 50.1 per cent. The senior notes are effectively subordinated to subsidiary obligations; guarantor terms and Terrion governance are not supplied [CP-1A: Transaction summary; Ownership and control].

runs.text: Scale and recurring earnings (Documentary Fact). TELUS Corporation earned LTM Adjusted EBITDA of C$ 7,315 million, and mobile network revenue of C$ 1,743 million in Q2 2026 compared with C$ 1,723 million a year earlier. Subscriber growth in mobile, connected devices and internet supports revenue visibility even with declining ARPU. This lowers the probability that operating earnings alone force a default; the weakness is pricing, not volume [CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A: Company and operating model].

Covenant headroom (Analyst Interpretation on documentary figures). Reported leverage of 3.5x sits 0.70x below the 4.25x limit, an EBITDA cushion of C$ 1,206 million (16.5 per cent) at constant net debt, and coverage of 4.9x sits 2.9x above the 2.00x floor. The covenants are not affected by goodwill revaluation, so the C$ 2,135 million impairment does not reduce headroom. This limits near-term acceleration risk, subject to unseen covenant definitions [CP-1: Covenant and liquidity position].

Liquidity and access (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Cash of C$ 1,387 million, revolver availability of C$ 657 million expiring August 2030, securitization availability of C$ 680 million and a non-revolving facility availability of C$ 344 million cover the issuer's stated objective of at least C$ 1 billion of available liquidity. The investment-grade wording from management supports commercial paper and bond access, though agency ratings are not supplied [CP-1: Covenant and liquidity position].

Management response (Management Language). The dividend reset, removal of the reinvestment plan discount and the end-2028 leverage target direct cash toward debt reduction, and junior subordinated notes and Terrion minority equity have reduced reported leverage. This improves debt service capacity if executed, but the savings figure is a management estimate [CP-1A: Capital allocation and disclosure].

Leverage above objective and definition-dependent (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Reported 3.5x exceeds the 2.5x to 3.0x range, gross leverage is 4.30x, and the equity credit on junior subordinated notes depends on agency treatment that is not supplied. If that treatment changed, reported leverage would move toward the gross figure and headroom would shrink [CP-1: Definitions review].

Falling cash interest cover (Documentary Fact). Cover declined from 5.31x to 4.62x over two quarters as interest paid rose, and junior subordinated notes carry coupons of 5.375 to 7.000 per cent. Refinancing of lower-coupon senior notes at current rates would add to interest, an inference the sources do not quantify [CP-1: Chart data interest cover; Debt register].

Weaker earnings momentum and guidance (Management Language and Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA fell, TELUS Digital Adjusted EBITDA was C$ 72 million against C$ 89 million, and management attributes the Digital weakness to demand ramp-downs and churn at certain hyperscale customers. Lower free cash flow guidance reduces internally funded deleveraging and increases reliance on asset sales [CP-1: Segment and KPI view; CP-1A: Company and operating model].

Distributions and capital intensity (Documentary Fact). Dividends declared were 109 per cent of cash from operations less capital expenditures over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, and capital expenditure guidance rose to about C$ 2.6 billion with a spectrum auction in October 2027. The dividend reset addresses the first point after quarter-end; the spectrum payment is a future call on cash [CP-1A: Governance and behaviour; Capital allocation].

Refinancing dependence (Analyst Interpretation). Current maturities of C$ 3,802 million include commercial paper of about C$ 2.1 billion (US$ 1.5 billion) that consumes revolver capacity one for one. Commercial paper itself depends on rollover, while other near-term maturities can draw on cash, securitization and bank facility availability or new issuance. Market closure would tighten liquidity quickly [CP-1: Chart data liquidity].

Structure and information (Insufficient Information). Guarantor terms, Terrion governance and its own debt, the audited annual statements and the credit agreements are not supplied. Missing evidence is not an adverse finding, but it prevents a view of loss given default or covenant robustness and keeps confidence at Medium [CP-0; CP-1A: Gaps].

runs.text: TELUS is not the subject of a sponsor buyout, merger or refinancing in the pinned sources, so no deal-level use of proceeds, sponsor or closing condition applies; one Insufficient Information row stands for any transaction after July 31, 2026, which is Not supplied. The completed transactions that shape the creditor's perimeter are these. First, the TELUS Digital privatization: on June 12, 2025 TELUS Corporation submitted a non-binding indication of interest to the board of TELUS International (Cda) Inc. [Q3FS page:63 "submitted a non-binding indication of interest"], signed a definitive agreement on September 2, 2025 at "for a price per share of US$4.50" [Q3FS page:64 "for a price per share of US$4.50"], payable in cash, Common Shares or a combination subject to a 25 per cent cap on shares, and closed on October 31, 2025 [Q3FS page:64 "The transaction closed October 31, 2025"]. The final cash and share mix and the cash outlay are Not supplied in the pinned sources. Second, Terrion: a wireless tower infrastructure partnership established on July 24, 2025 that issued equity to an outside holder for net cash proceeds of 1,246 [Q3FS page:65 "Net cash proceeds $ 1,261"], after which TELUS keeps 50.1 per cent voting and economic interest and holds a call option exercisable in whole in September 2027 if there is a partner dispute or after September 2057 at generally the greater of fair value and a multiple on invested capital [Q3FS page:64 "call option"]. The outside holder is not named in the pinned sources. The Terrion non-controlling interest was 792 at September 30, 2025 and non-controlling interests were 808 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Third, Workplace Options: TELUS acquired 100 per cent on May 1, 2025 [Q3FS page:44 "On May 1, 2025, we acquired 100% of Workplace Options"], with cash consideration of 453 funded in part by 280 (US$200 million) of preferred shares issued by a subsidiary to a private equity investor; the preferred shares were later exchanged for a US$200 million promissory note and the note was repaid in Q2 2026 with a prepayment premium of 51 (CP-1). Fourth, liability management: tender offers in June and December 2025 that bought back senior notes (series CL, CU, CW, CAB, CAE and U.S. dollar notes), with gains on purchase of long-term debt of 222 in Q3 2025 and 81 in Q4 2025 [MDA2Q26 page:29 "Gain on purchase of long-term debt"], the full redemption of the 3.75% Series CV notes on January 16, 2026, the redemption of 500 of the 2.75% Series CZ notes on May 8, 2026, and the payment of the remaining 300 of that series at maturity after June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Fifth, equity and distributions: the dividend reset announced July 31, 2026 and the end of the dividend reinvestment plan discount effective October 1, 2026 [REL2Q26 page:4 "representing a reset of 55 per cent to an annualized amount of $0.75 per share"]; no shares were repurchased under the normal course issuer bid in the quarter [MDA2Q26 page:26 "we did not repurchase or cancel any shares pursuant to our NCIB"]. Sixth, asset monetization: management says it is in discussions on TELUS Health non-core assets and is advancing the monetization of non-core real estate, with proceeds directed to debt reduction [REL2Q26 page:4 "the company remains active in the market on TELUS Health-related non-core assets"]. Assets, buyers, prices and timing are Not supplied, so no leverage effect can be estimated.

New debt issues in the pinned sources, as printed in the March 31, 2026 debt note (all unsecured and issued by TELUS Corporation unless stated): fixed-to-fixed rate junior subordinated notes issued in 2025 and December 2025 comprising Series CAR 6.25 per cent (1,500 outstanding, due July 2055), Series CAS 6.75 per cent (925, due July 2055), U.S. dollar Series A 6.625 per cent (US$700 million, due October 2055), Series B 7.000 per cent (US$800 million, due October 2055), Series C 6.375 per cent (US$800 million, due June 2056), Series D 6.625 per cent (US$700 million, due June 2056), Series CAT 5.375 per cent (400, due June 2056) and Series CAU 5.875 per cent (400, due June 2056) [Q1FS page:45 "Series CAT"]. The Series C, D, CAT and CAU notes were issued in December 2025. The junior subordinated notes are subordinated to all senior indebtedness, receive one-half equity credit in leverage ratios in the initial post-issuance decade, and carry a repurchase offer at 102 per cent upon a rating event (CP-1). No new senior note series issued in the first half of 2026 is itemized in the pinned sources; long-term debt issued in that half is described in the MD&A mainly as commercial paper activity with a commercial paper balance of $2.1 billion (US$1.5 billion) at June 30, 2026 [MDA2Q26 page:56 "a balance of $2.1 billion (US$1.5 billion) at June 30, 2026"]. Sustainability-linked note series (CAF, CAG, CAJ, CAK, CAN and the 3.40 per cent U.S. dollar series) were issued before 2025 and the debt table refers to trigger events and step-ups for them (CP-1 debt register).

fields.value: TELUS is a large, investment-grade-rated Canadian telecommunications issuer whose reported leverage is 3.5 times net debt to EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs at June 30, 2026, above both its previous and its newly set objective ranges, but below the covenant limit of 4.25 times. The financial base can be built from the pinned sources for the latest quarter and for four consecutive balance sheet dates, with limits. Reported leverage depends on a definition that gives half equity credit to the junior subordinated notes and adjusts for hedging items, so a gross view is also shown: total debt, including lease liabilities and short-term borrowings, is 4.30 times LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs. Cash interest cover on the same EBITDA is 4.62 times, down from 5.09 times a quarter earlier, partly because cash interest paid in Q2 2026 included a prepayment premium. Liquidity at June 30, 2026 is cash and temporary investments of 1,387, revolver availability of 657 after a 2,093 commercial paper backstop, securitization availability of 680 and a further 344 on a non-revolving bank facility due June 2027. Current maturities of long-term debt are 3,802. The second quarter brought a 2,135 impairment relating to TELUS Digital, a net loss of 1,830, a dividend reset and lower guidance. The view is restricted by missing audited FY2025 statements, missing second-quarter notes and missing agreements, so FY2025 flows are assembled from quarters and the debt register is dated March 31, 2026. fields.value: - Leverage is definition-dependent. Evidence: net debt of 25,963 uses half equity credit for junior subordinated notes and EBITDA of 7,315. Mechanism: the notes are subordinated and carry a rating-event repurchase at 102 per cent, so the equity credit depends on agency treatment; if lost, reported leverage rises toward the gross figure. Implication: senior creditors should monitor the gross ratio of 4.30 times as well as the covenant ratio, because covenant headroom is 0.70 times on the issuer's own definition.

fields.value: - Cash interest cover is moving down. Evidence: EBITDA over cash interest paid fell from 5.31 at FY2025 to 4.62 at June 30, 2026. Mechanism: interest paid rose by 142 in Q2 2026 and 201 in H1 2026 on 2025 junior subordinated issuance, the promissory note and the prepayment premium, while LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs fell from 7,354 to 7,315. Implication: cash cover has less margin, although part of the Q2 2026 rise is one-off.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing and liquidity. Evidence: current maturities of long-term debt of 3,802, commercial paper of 2.1 billion fully backstopped by a revolver with 657 availability. Mechanism: commercial paper is classified as current but is supported by the revolver, so it consumes revolver capacity one for one and the availability of 657 is what remains after that backstop. The other current maturities, including the US$600 million 2.80% notes reclassified to current and the Series CZ balance paid in July 2026, rely on cash of 1,387, securitization availability of 680, non-revolving availability of 344 or new issuance. Implication: near-term maturities depend on commercial paper rollover and market access; the investment-grade wording supports access but ratings are not supplied and not tested here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings quality. Evidence: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 1,777 versus 1,812 and a 2,135 non-cash impairment; Digital Adjusted EBITDA 72 versus 89. Mechanism: the impairment does not affect EBITDA or covenants, which are not impacted by revaluation of goodwill [MDA2Q26 page:61 "The covenants are not impacted by revaluation"], but signals lower recoverable value in the TELUS Digital unit. Implication: covenant headroom is unaffected by the impairment, while the lower guidance affects forward leverage.

fields.value: TELUS Corporation is a British Columbia company and one of Canada's largest telecommunications groups, with three reporting segments: TELUS technology solutions (mobile, fixed data and voice, security and automation, agriculture and consumer goods technology), TELUS Health (employee and family assistance programs, benefits administration, virtual care) and TELUS Digital (digital solutions, AI and data, trust and safety, customer experience management). The sources describe no controlling shareholder, no sponsor and no pending change of control; ownership detail beyond the share count and a Canadian-ownership voting restriction is not supplied. The creditor-relevant structure is a parent that issues all identified senior notes, commercial paper and junior subordinated notes and is effectively subordinated to obligations of, or guaranteed by, its subsidiaries, with a subsidiary (Terrion) holding minority outside equity. The relevant history is a 2025 reshaping of the perimeter: the acquisition of Workplace Options in May 2025, the establishment of Terrion in July 2025 with outside equity, and the buy-in of the TELUS Digital minority on October 31, 2025, followed in 2026 by a 2,135 impairment of TELUS Digital, a management transition, a dividend reset, lower guidance and asset sale processes. Business risk is anchored by a large mobile and fibre base with declining ARPU at a decelerating rate, partly offset by growth in connected devices and internet connections. As an analyst reading, TELUS Digital depends on external clients and intersegment work, and Health earnings were built partly by acquisition. The view is restricted by the absence of the annual information form, the transaction agreements and any filing after July 31, 2026.

fields.value: TELUS is not the subject of a sponsor buyout, merger or refinancing in the pinned sources, so no deal-level use of proceeds, sponsor or closing condition applies; one Insufficient Information row stands for any transaction after July 31, 2026, which is Not supplied. The completed transactions that shape the creditor's perimeter are these. First, the TELUS Digital privatization: on June 12, 2025 TELUS Corporation submitted a non-binding indication of interest to the board of TELUS International (Cda) Inc. [Q3FS page:63 "submitted a non-binding indication of interest"], signed a definitive agreement on September 2, 2025 at "for a price per share of US$4.50" [Q3FS page:64 "for a price per share of US$4.50"], payable in cash, Common Shares or a combination subject to a 25 per cent cap on shares, and closed on October 31, 2025 [Q3FS page:64 "The transaction closed October 31, 2025"]. The final cash and share mix and the cash outlay are Not supplied in the pinned sources. Second, Terrion: a wireless tower infrastructure partnership established on July 24, 2025 that issued equity to an outside holder for net cash proceeds of 1,246 [Q3FS page:65 "Net cash proceeds $ 1,261"], after which TELUS keeps 50.1 per cent voting and economic interest and holds a call option exercisable in whole in September 2027 if there is a partner dispute or after September 2057 at generally the greater of fair value and a multiple on invested capital [Q3FS page:64 "call option"]. The outside holder is not named in the pinned sources. The Terrion non-controlling interest was 792 at September 30, 2025 and non-controlling interests were 808 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Third, Workplace Options: TELUS acquired 100 per cent on May 1, 2025 [Q3FS page:44 "On May 1, 2025, we acquired 100% of Workplace Options"], with cash consideration of 453 funded in part by 280 (US$200 million) of preferred shares issued by a subsidiary to a private equity investor; the preferred shares were later exchanged for a US$200 million promissory note and the note was repaid in Q2 2026 with a prepayment premium of 51 (CP-1). Fourth, liability management: tender offers in June and December 2025 that bought back senior notes (series CL, CU, CW, CAB, CAE and U.S. dollar notes), with gains on purchase of long-term debt of 222 in Q3 2025 and 81 in Q4 2025 [MDA2Q26 page:29 "Gain on purchase of long-term debt"], the full redemption of the 3.75% Series CV notes on January 16, 2026, the redemption of 500 of the 2.75% Series CZ notes on May 8, 2026, and the payment of the remaining 300 of that series at maturity after June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Fifth, equity and distributions: the dividend reset announced July 31, 2026 and the end of the dividend reinvestment plan discount effective October 1, 2026 [REL2Q26 page:4 "representing a reset of 55 per cent to an annualized amount of $0.75 per share"]; no shares were repurchased under the normal course issuer bid in the quarter [MDA2Q26 page:26 "we did not repurchase or cancel any shares pursuant to our NCIB"]. Sixth, asset monetization: management says it is in discussions on TELUS Health non-core assets and is advancing the monetization of non-core real estate, with proceeds directed to debt reduction [REL2Q26 page:4 "the company remains active in the market on TELUS Health-related non-core assets"]. Assets, buyers, prices and timing are Not supplied, so no leverage effect can be estimated.

fields.value: 1. Perimeter and structural subordination. Evidence: the buy-in of the TELUS Digital minority closed October 31, 2025 and Terrion has outside equity with TELUS holding 50.1 per cent [Q3FS page:64 "retained a 50.1% voting and economic interest in Terrion"]; the senior notes are effectively subordinated to obligations of, or guaranteed by, subsidiaries (CP-1). Mechanism: cash generated in Terrion is shared with the outside holder, and any creditors of Terrion (its own debt is Not supplied) would rank ahead of the parent's notes, while TELUS Digital cash flows now fully accrue to the group but carry impairment and demand risk. Implication: a creditor of the parent depends on upstreaming from subsidiaries; guarantor and Terrion terms are Not supplied, so the structural position cannot be completed. The counter-evidence is that the parent issues all identified senior debt and TELUS Communications Inc. and TELUS Health Inc. are wholly owned.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Revenue durability and margin. Evidence: mobile network revenue 1,743 against 1,723, fixed data services 1,175 against 1,170, TELUS Digital revenue down to 774 from 827, and ARPU declining at a decelerating rate. Mechanism: growth is subscriber-led with flat unit pricing, so incremental margin depends on cost programs, which management has enlarged (restructuring assumption of approximately $900 million). Implication: free cash flow is exposed to price competition and Digital demand; management lowered 2026 guidance. The counter-evidence is subscriber growth in connected devices and internet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Capital allocation and deleveraging path. Evidence: dividend reset, capital expenditures guidance of approximately $2.6 billion, asset sale processes without terms, and a leverage target moved to year-end 2028. Mechanism: debt reduction depends on lower dividends and unquantified proceeds while capital intensity is higher in 2026 and a spectrum auction follows in October 2027. Implication: leverage tolerance is limited near term; monitor the next release for the capital returns framework and any asset sale agreements. The counter-evidence is the investment-grade wording and covenant headroom reported in CP-1.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Regulatory risk to revenue durability. Evidence: the wholesale fibre access framework requires aggregated access to TELUS fibre networks and is under appeal, with hearings likely late 2026 or early 2027 [MDA2Q26 page:67 "The appeal and judicial review will be heard together, likely in late 2026 or early 2027"]. Mechanism (analyst interpretation): wholesale access can reduce retail fibre share and price. Implication: outcome is uncertain and unquantified in the pinned sources; the issuer does not state a financial effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TELUS Corporation is a large Canadian telecommunications borrower whose credit is sound on liquidity and covenants today but weakening in direction. The strongest support is scale and recurring mobile and fibre earnings (LTM Adjusted EBITDA C$ 7,315 million), a reported leverage ratio of 3.5x against a 4.25x covenant, cash of C$ 1,387 million, C$ 657 million of revolver availability to 2030 and investment-grade rating wording. The weakest point is leverage: reported 3.5x relies on half equity credit for C$ 7,322 million of junior subordinated notes, gross debt to EBITDA is 4.30x, cash interest cover fell to 4.62x and 2026 guidance was cut. What decides the outcome is whether the dividend reset, capital discipline and unquantified asset sales bring leverage toward the year-end 2028 target while commercial paper and bond markets remain open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, leverage is the central issue and depends on definition. Net debt of C$ 25,963 million over LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs of C$ 7,315 million is 3.55x unrounded (3.5x as reported), above the issuer's new 2.5x to 3.0x objective range, and below the 4.25x covenant limit by 0.70x on the issuer's own measure. The issuer gives one-half equity credit to its junior subordinated notes; gross debt of C$ 31,456 million is 4.30x LTM EBITDA, and before the equity credit net debt was 4.02x at March 31, 2026. The covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is indicative [CP-1: Chart data leverage; Definitions review].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, cash interest cover is declining. LTM EBITDA over cash interest paid was 4.62x at June 30, 2026, 5.09x at March 31, 2026 and 5.31x at FY2025. Interest paid rose on 2025 junior subordinated issuance, a promissory note and a C$ 51 million prepayment premium, so part of the fall is one-off; the issuer's own coverage measure is 4.9x against a 2.00x covenant floor [CP-1: Chart data interest cover].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, liquidity is adequate; refinancing relies on market access. Cash is C$ 1,387 million, revolver availability C$ 657 million after a C$ 2,093 million commercial paper backstop, securitization availability C$ 680 million and a non-revolving facility C$ 344 million. Current maturities of long-term debt are C$ 3,802 million and include commercial paper that the revolver supports. The maturity schedule, dated March 31, 2026, shows C$ 3,148 million falling due in the rest of 2026, C$ 1,928 million in 2027 and C$ 2,319 million in 2028 [CP-1: Chart data liquidity and debt maturities].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, earnings and guidance weakened in the quarter. Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was C$ 1,777 million against C$ 1,812 million, with a net loss of C$ 1,830 million after a C$ 2,135 million non-cash TELUS Digital impairment, which does not touch covenants. Management lowered 2026 guidance: service revenue flat to a 2 per cent decline, Adjusted EBITDA down 2 to 4 per cent, free cash flow about C$ 1.8 billion from about C$ 2.45 billion, and capital expenditures about C$ 2.6 billion from about C$ 2.3 billion (Management Language) [CP-1: Subsequent events and guidance].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the deleveraging plan rests on management actions rather than organic cash flow. The quarterly dividend was reset to C$ 0.1875 per share from C$ 0.4184, with management estimating about C$ 2.7 billion of cash savings through 2028; the 3.0x target date moved from year-end 2027 to year-end 2028 and the objective range moved from 2.2x to 2.7x to 2.5x to 3.0x. Asset sales of TELUS Health non-core assets and real estate are under way with no assets, prices or timing supplied [CP-1A: Capital allocation; Conflicts].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the perimeter changed in 2025 and structural position is incomplete. TELUS bought out the TELUS Digital minority on October 31, 2025 and sold minority equity in the Terrion tower partnership for net cash proceeds of C$ 1,246 million while keeping 50.1 per cent. The senior notes are effectively subordinated to subsidiary obligations; guarantor terms and Terrion governance are not supplied [CP-1A: Transaction summary; Ownership and control].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and recurring earnings (Documentary Fact). TELUS Corporation earned LTM Adjusted EBITDA of C$ 7,315 million, and mobile network revenue of C$ 1,743 million in Q2 2026 compared with C$ 1,723 million a year earlier. Subscriber growth in mobile, connected devices and internet supports revenue visibility even with declining ARPU. This lowers the probability that operating earnings alone force a default; the weakness is pricing, not volume [CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A: Company and operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant headroom (Analyst Interpretation on documentary figures). Reported leverage of 3.5x sits 0.70x below the 4.25x limit, an EBITDA cushion of C$ 1,206 million (16.5 per cent) at constant net debt, and coverage of 4.9x sits 2.9x above the 2.00x floor. The covenants are not affected by goodwill revaluation, so the C$ 2,135 million impairment does not reduce headroom. This limits near-term acceleration risk, subject to unseen covenant definitions [CP-1: Covenant and liquidity position].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and access (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Cash of C$ 1,387 million, revolver availability of C$ 657 million expiring August 2030, securitization availability of C$ 680 million and a non-revolving facility availability of C$ 344 million cover the issuer's stated objective of at least C$ 1 billion of available liquidity. The investment-grade wording from management supports commercial paper and bond access, though agency ratings are not supplied [CP-1: Covenant and liquidity position].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management response (Management Language). The dividend reset, removal of the reinvestment plan discount and the end-2028 leverage target direct cash toward debt reduction, and junior subordinated notes and Terrion minority equity have reduced reported leverage. This improves debt service capacity if executed, but the savings figure is a management estimate [CP-1A: Capital allocation and disclosure].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage above objective and definition-dependent (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Reported 3.5x exceeds the 2.5x to 3.0x range, gross leverage is 4.30x, and the equity credit on junior subordinated notes depends on agency treatment that is not supplied. If that treatment changed, reported leverage would move toward the gross figure and headroom would shrink [CP-1: Definitions review].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Falling cash interest cover (Documentary Fact). Cover declined from 5.31x to 4.62x over two quarters as interest paid rose, and junior subordinated notes carry coupons of 5.375 to 7.000 per cent. Refinancing of lower-coupon senior notes at current rates would add to interest, an inference the sources do not quantify [CP-1: Chart data interest cover; Debt register].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaker earnings momentum and guidance (Management Language and Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA fell, TELUS Digital Adjusted EBITDA was C$ 72 million against C$ 89 million, and management attributes the Digital weakness to demand ramp-downs and churn at certain hyperscale customers. Lower free cash flow guidance reduces internally funded deleveraging and increases reliance on asset sales [CP-1: Segment and KPI view; CP-1A: Company and operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distributions and capital intensity (Documentary Fact). Dividends declared were 109 per cent of cash from operations less capital expenditures over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, and capital expenditure guidance rose to about C$ 2.6 billion with a spectrum auction in October 2027. The dividend reset addresses the first point after quarter-end; the spectrum payment is a future call on cash [CP-1A: Governance and behaviour; Capital allocation].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing dependence (Analyst Interpretation). Current maturities of C$ 3,802 million include commercial paper of about C$ 2.1 billion (US$ 1.5 billion) that consumes revolver capacity one for one. Commercial paper itself depends on rollover, while other near-term maturities can draw on cash, securitization and bank facility availability or new issuance. Market closure would tighten liquidity quickly [CP-1: Chart data liquidity].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure and information (Insufficient Information). Guarantor terms, Terrion governance and its own debt, the audited annual statements and the credit agreements are not supplied. Missing evidence is not an adverse finding, but it prevents a view of loss given default or covenant robustness and keeps confidence at Medium [CP-0; CP-1A: Gaps].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TELUS Corporation is a scale telecommunications borrower with adequate liquidity and covenant headroom whose credit quality is under pressure from above-objective, definition-dependent leverage, falling cash interest cover and lowered guidance, so the outcome depends on delivering dividend-funded deleveraging and asset sales while market access stays open (Analyst Interpretation).
